source.title: Holistic Audit Dataset Generation for LLM Unlearning via Knowledge Graph Traversal and Redundancy Removal
source.authors: Wei-Peng Jiang; Juan Zhai; Shiqing Ma; Ziyan Lei; Xiao-Fei Xie; Yi-Ge Wang; Chao Shen

record.tranche_reason: The study uses a new, expanded audit set to measure knowledge memorization after unlearning; it does not test recovery attacks.
record.gate_note: The reported KMC counts for unlearned models bear on residual targeted knowledge. The paper does not test fine-tuning recovery, activation ablation, quantization, prompt-based recovery, or a counter-method. HANKER-versus-MUSE comparisons report the same memorization measures under different audit suites. The redundancy-cleaning comparisons in §4.4 concern changes to audit-set composition and metric inflation, not recovery attacks.
record.test_reason: The study re-audits MUSE-unlearned LLaMA2-7B models with a 69k/111k-question fact-level suite. It finds thousands of forget-set facts still answered correctly, arguing that unlearning success is an artifact of small audits. This bears on whether targeted knowledge reaches near-zero (Version A). It tests no recovery attack (B–E) and no robust counter-method (F).
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that HANKER's audit detects far more memorization cases than MUSE (142–1,242× per their §4.3), so current unlearning may be less effective than believed. They also conclude that forget/retain redundancy produces false-positive memorization cases and inflates dataset-level ROUGE/entailment, so deduplication is needed for accurate assessment.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates MUSE-provided GA, NPO, and Task Vector implementations using a newly generated audit suite; it does not reproduce the recovery attacks in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by unlearning method, dataset, audit suite, and metric.
record.problems: The paper evaluates only MUSE datasets and uses DeepSeek-V3 for question generation. Manual knowledge-fact accuracy is reported as 0.76 for News and 0.61 for Books. No chance level or general-ability result is given, and no recovery attack is tested.
record.rows_left_out: Section 4.4 and Figure 4 compare audit-set cleaning and report changes in KMC detection and dataset-level ROUGE/Entailment metrics. They are omitted because they concern redundancy's effect on audit metrics rather than a recovery intervention.

untested.parts: Preservation of general ability or utility; no chance or retrained-model baseline; whether simple attacks recover the knowledge.
No activation ablation and no blocking-vs-deletion analysis.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context recovery; the audit questions are plain direct queries.

missing.what: Audit-suite sizes, needed to convert KMC counts to rates: 69,609 QA pairs for News and 111,855 for Books. The rows give raw counts only.

record.verdict_notes: The paper is not one of the originals. Main caveats: there is no chance or retrained-model baseline, so some KMCs may be general knowledge the base model would answer anyway. Knowledge-fact accuracy is only 0.76 (News) and 0.61 (Books). Results come from a single model (LLaMA2-7B) with MUSE default scripts, and no uncertainty is reported. The paper's '10^3×' headline does not exactly match its own reported ratios. The §4.4 cleaning comparison is correctly declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: The study measures residual knowledge after unlearning, but does not report near-chance accuracy, preserved general ability, or whether simple attacks recover knowledge.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of access blocking versus knowledge deletion.
No prompt rephrasing, jailbreak, language variation, or in-context recovery test.
No method is tested for resisting recovery attacks.

relationships.condition: HANKER audit: NPO-GDR on News; Task Vector on News and Books
relationships.reason: KMC counts stay within about 5% of the non-unlearned model, or rise slightly; thousands of facts remain answerable (r09, r10, r17, r18, r37, r38).
relationships.display_finding: Answerable factual knowledge remained within about 5% of the original model or increased slightly, leaving thousands of facts accessible.

relationships.condition: HANKER audit: GA-KLR and NPO-KLR on News and Books; NPO-GDR on Books
relationships.reason: Counts fall by roughly 8–70% but thousands of memorization cases remain (e.g., NPO-GDR Books 1435 ROUGE / 18094 entailment), far from removal (r05, r06, r13, r14, r25, r26, r29, r30, r33, r34).
relationships.display_finding: Memorization declined approximately 8–70%, but thousands of cases remained, including 1435 ROUGE matches and 18094 entailment cases for NPO-GDR Books.

relationships.reason: Pre-unlearning counts are only 15–33, so apparent success rests on few cases. Results are mixed: NPO-GDR Books ROUGE reaches 0 (r31), but entailment rises 15→34 (r32) and Task Vector is unchanged (r19, r39, r40).
relationships.display_finding: The original audit found only 15–33 cases before unlearning; NPO-GDR Books reduced ROUGE matches to zero but increased entailment cases from 15 to 34, while Task Vector left memorization unchanged.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: HANKER audit, News and Books; GA-KLR, NPO-GDR, and NPO-KLR
reader_labels.reason: The audit still finds many KMCs after these unlearning methods, though counts are below the unlearned reference; the paper gives no chance-level comparison (r05-r06, r09-r10, r13-r14, r25-r26, r29-r30, r33-r34).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Task Vector on HANKER News and Books
reader_labels.reason: The detected KMC counts are close to the unlearned reference, and are higher than it on News, rather than indicating a substantial reduction in detected knowledge (r17-r18, r37-r38).
